title: Cabinet Temperature Probe Open / Failed
shortDescription: The cabinet (air) temperature thermistor is reading open circuit or out of range.
fullDescription:
True commercial refrigerators use an NTC thermistor inside the cabinet to report air temperature to the electronic controller. PRB1 indicates the controller has lost valid input from this probe — either an open circuit, shorted wire, or thermistor drift outside the acceptable resistance range. Most T-Series and GDM merchandisers will run a failsafe duty cycle while the fault is active, which can lead to excessive cycling or product warming.

This code appears on the LED temperature display of the Lauren controller typically used in T-23, T-49, T-72, GDM-26, and GDM-49 units. You must clear the condition and reset power or the unit will continue default-cycling the compressor.

causes.cause: Cabinet thermistor physically damaged or pinched by product

symptoms: Compressor runs constant or default cycle

fixSteps.title: Verify probe location
fixSteps.instruction: Open cabinet and locate air sensor clipped near the evaporator return. Inspect for crushing or ice encasement.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect probe at controller, measure resistance with multimeter. At 38F should read approximately 30 kOhm; open or infinite = bad probe.

fixSteps.title: Replace probe
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching True OEM cabinet probe, route away from sharp edges, reclip in original bracket.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech for warranty on sealed system and 24/7 uptime critical in foodservice.
videoSearchQuery: True refrigeration PRB1 cabinet probe fault

faq.q: Will the unit keep cooling with PRB1 active?
faq.a: Yes, it runs a default duty cycle, but temperature accuracy is lost — verify with an independent thermometer.

faq.q: Is PRB1 the evap coil probe?
faq.a: No — PRB1 is the air/cabinet probe. Evap coil probe faults are reported as PRB2.

title: Evaporator Coil Probe Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil defrost-termination probe is open or reading invalid.
fullDescription:
PRB2 refers to the coil probe that senses evaporator temperature and terminates defrost when the coil has warmed enough to melt accumulated frost. When this input is lost, the controller may use a time-only defrost and risks coil icing or prolonged defrost heat, which warms product.

Commonly seen on T-Series solid-door reach-ins after the unit has been moved or the evap coil has been cleaned — the probe clip can pop off or the harness gets snagged on fan shrouds.

fixSteps.title: Remove evap cover
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off power. Remove fan shroud screws and inspect probe clip position on the evaporator return bend.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and ohm the probe cold; an open reading confirms failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace and re-clip
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM probe, secure to coil with factory clip, dress harness clear of fan blades.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — probe is behind the evaporator and requires confident electrical work.
videoSearchQuery: True T-49 PRB2 evaporator probe replace

faq.q: How often should evap probe clips be checked?
faq.a: Every time the evaporator is cleaned — every 3-6 months in busy kitchens.

title: High Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Cabinet temperature exceeded the high-temperature setpoint for longer than the delay period.
fullDescription:
HtA indicates cabinet temperature has risen above the high alarm threshold (factory default typically 45F for refrigerators, 10F for freezers) for longer than the alarm delay (often 60 minutes). The alarm continues after the unit recovers until manually cleared on some models.

Common triggers include doors left open during a rush, dirty condenser, low refrigerant charge, evaporator icing, and failed evaporator fan. For True GDM glass-door merchandisers this alarm is especially frequent because heavy customer traffic repeatedly opens the doors.

causes.cause: Door gasket leak or door left ajar

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Power off. Remove front grille and vacuum/brush the condenser coil thoroughly. Restore power.

fixSteps.title: Check door seals
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect gaskets for tears or compression set. Test seal with a dollar bill — should have noticeable drag when pulled.

fixSteps.title: Verify evap fan
fixSteps.instruction: With doors open and safety switch defeated per service manual, confirm evaporator fans spin freely and run during compressor cycle.

fixSteps.title: Call refrigeration tech if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning and door seals are fine but HtA returns, likely refrigerant charge issue — requires EPA-certified technician.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — sealed system diagnosis requires EPA 608 certification.
videoSearchQuery: True refrigerator HtA high temp alarm fix

faq.q: How do I silence the alarm?
faq.a: Press and hold the mute button on the Lauren controller; the alarm will resume if the condition persists.

title: Low Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Cabinet temperature dropped below the low-temperature alarm setpoint.
fullDescription:
LtA fires when the cabinet runs colder than the low alarm threshold — common on refrigerators when the compressor fails to cycle off (stuck contactor, welded relay) or the temperature probe has drifted low. For freezers this may indicate a defrost termination problem leaving the evaporator excessively cold.

Freezing product in a refrigerator is an operational concern — produce and dairy can be damaged.

fixSteps.title: Verify setpoint
fixSteps.instruction: Check controller setpoint is 36-38F for refrigerators.

fixSteps.title: Rearrange product
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure product does not block evaporator return air or the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Test compressor contactor
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle power; if compressor does not stop when setpoint is reached, replace contactor/relay.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech when compressor circuit is suspect.
videoSearchQuery: True LtA low temp alarm commercial fridge

faq.q: Is frozen lettuce a warranty claim?
faq.a: Product loss typically is not covered; the equipment repair may be.

title: Defrost Cycle Active or Fault
shortDescription: Unit is in defrost or a defrost termination fault has occurred.
fullDescription:
dEF on the display normally indicates the unit is performing a scheduled off-cycle or heated defrost and is expected behavior. If dEF remains for more than the maximum defrost duration (typically 30-45 minutes), the controller has failed to terminate defrost — usually due to a failed heater, stuck defrost relay, or bad coil probe.

For True freezer models (T-49F, T-72F, GDM-49F), prolonged defrost warms the evaporator and can lead to product thaw if ignored.

fixSteps.title: Wait out normal cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Allow up to 30 minutes for normal defrost to complete.

fixSteps.title: Test defrost heater
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, access evap, measure heater resistance — should read finite ohms; open = failed.

fixSteps.title: Replace heater or probe
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM part; verify drain line is clear of ice.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — working inside a freezer evap during thaw can be slippery and electrical.
videoSearchQuery: True freezer dEF defrost stuck fix

faq.a: Factory default is typically 4 times in 24 hours for freezers.

title: Compressor Fault
shortDescription: Compressor has failed to start, overheated, or tripped internal overload repeatedly.
fullDescription:
CFA is logged when the controller detects repeated compressor start failures, short cycling, or overload trip events. Root causes range from dirty condensers causing high head pressure to failed start components (capacitor, relay) or a mechanically stuck compressor.

This is a serious code — continued attempts to restart a failed compressor will damage it and the start components.
symptoms: Compressor clicks but does not start

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser and verify airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, clean condenser thoroughly, ensure at least 3 inches of air clearance at rear.

fixSteps.title: Test start components
fixSteps.instruction: Check capacitor with meter, inspect start relay for burn marks.

fixSteps.title: Call refrigeration tech
fixSteps.instruction: If compressor draws locked-rotor amps, compressor replacement is required — EPA 608 work.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — sealed-system work is EPA-regulated.
videoSearchQuery: True refrigerator CFA compressor fault diagnose

faq.q: Can I run the unit while waiting for parts?
faq.a: No — transfer product to another unit, repeated start attempts will kill the compressor.

title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: Evaporator fan motor has stalled, drawn excessive current, or reported a tachometer fault.
fullDescription: Newer True models with ECM evaporator fans monitor fan speed via a tach signal. EFA indicates the fan is not spinning at commanded RPM — due to ice blocking the blade, failed motor, or harness issue. Without evap airflow, the coil ices quickly and cabinet temp rises.

fixSteps.title: Full defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and let unit thaw completely; clear drain.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Spin blade by hand — should be free. If gritty or seized, replace motor.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech if the coil must be removed.
videoSearchQuery: True refrigeration EFA evaporator fan motor

faq.q: Can I use a generic fan motor?
faq.a: Only an ECM-compatible replacement with matching tach signal will clear EFA.

title: Condenser High Temperature
shortDescription: Condenser-coil or discharge temperature probe reports an overheating condition.
fullDescription: CtA warns that the condenser section is running too hot. Most commonly this is a dirty condenser or blocked airflow — common in bakeries, pizza kitchens, and anywhere ambient is high. Persistent CtA will lead to compressor overload trips and eventual compressor damage.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove grille, vacuum and brush the condenser.

fixSteps.title: Verify condenser fan
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fan spins during compressor run; replace motor if seized.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech when the fan is integrated into the top deck.
videoSearchQuery: True refrigerator CtA condenser high temp

faq.q: How often should the condenser be cleaned?
faq.a: Monthly minimum; weekly in greasy environments.

title: Door Open Alarm
shortDescription: One or more doors have been open beyond the allowed time (typically 3-5 minutes).
fullDescription:
The door alarm uses a reed switch (magnet on door, switch on frame) to detect open doors. A door-open event exceeding the alarm delay triggers visual and audible alarms. Common on busy GDM merchandisers and prep tables.

If no door is actually open, the reed switch or its magnet alignment is likely the problem.

fixSteps.title: Physically confirm door closed
fixSteps.instruction: Close and latch all doors; gasket should fully compress.

fixSteps.title: Test reed switch
fixSteps.instruction: Pass a magnet across the switch location; alarm should clear. If not, replace switch.

whenToCallPro: Usually a DIY fix; call pro if switch is buried in cabinet frame.
videoSearchQuery: True refrigerator door alarm switch replace

faq.q: Can I disable the door alarm?
faq.a: Not recommended — it protects product during rushes.

title: Controller Communication Error
shortDescription: Main controller has lost communication with the user display board.
fullDescription: E1 on True smart-controller models indicates loss of communication between the main control board and the front display interface. Usually a ribbon/harness issue, moisture ingress, or a failed display board.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug unit 60 seconds and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Open display bezel, reseat ribbon between display and main board.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — display boards are keyed to models.
videoSearchQuery: True Spec Series E1 communication error

faq.q: Does unit cool while E1 active?
faq.a: Often yes — the main board runs defaults — but you cannot change setpoint.

title: Low Voltage / Brownout Warning
shortDescription: Incoming line voltage has dropped below the safe operating range.
fullDescription:
Some True controllers monitor supply voltage; LO warns of brownout conditions that could damage the compressor. The controller inhibits compressor start until voltage recovers.

Common in kitchens during heavy equipment startup or generator operation.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage at receptacle
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 115V (or 208/230V per model) at receptacle with unit running.

fixSteps.title: Call electrician
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is low, the issue is building wiring — not the refrigerator.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — supply voltage issues require a licensed electrician.

faq.a: A voltage-monitoring power conditioner can help; a simple surge strip will not.

title: Drain Line Freeze Up
shortDescription: Condensate drain line frozen, water pooling in cabinet.
fullDescription: dF (on newer Spec Series with water sensor) warns that defrost water is not draining — typically because the drain heater has failed or the drain line is iced. Left alone, water pools and freezes, eventually flooding the cabinet floor.

fixSteps.title: Thaw drain line
fixSteps.instruction: Power off unit, allow full thaw, flush drain with warm water.

fixSteps.title: Test drain heater
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm out the drain line heater; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — drain heater replacement means accessing evaporator section.
videoSearchQuery: True freezer dF drain line freeze repair

faq.a: Defrost water leaves the coil warm but refreezes in a cold drain line if the drain heater is not working.
